newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - AT&T up in active trade.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - AT&T up in active trade.

text.p: AT&T Corp rose in pre-open trade Tuesday boosted by a report it was in merger talks with SBC Communications Inc for a deal estimated to be worth at least $50 billion, traders said.
Stock in AT&T, the United States' biggest telecom carrier, was at 36-3/4, up from its Friday close of 36-1/8.
"It's by far the most active" share, a trader said.
SBC, owner of the Southwestern Bell and Pacific Telesis local phone systems, was not trading, but "buyers are lining up," he said. The shares closed Friday at 56-7/8.
The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday AT&T and SBC were in talks for a merger worth more than $50 billion. If completed, the deal would be the largest corporate combination in history.
An AT&T spokeswomen declined to comment on the report.
LHS Group Inc, a provider of billing and customer care software to telecommunications companies, jumped to 35-3/4 from a Friday close of 30-3/8.
A trader said the company had contracts with a unit of SBC and added, "It could be a big winner in the merger. I don't know."
Among other active shares, Micron Technologies Inc was up at 39-1/4 from a Friday close of 38-1/4. Merrill Lynch raised its 1997 and 1998 EPS view and 18-month price target.

FSI International Inc fell to an offered price of 13-7/8 from a Friday close of 14-3/8. The maker of equipment for processing silicon wafers said it expected a net loss for the third quarter of $0.10 to $0.15 a share.
Sun Microsystems Inc was at 34-1/2 from a Friday close of 33-7/8.
